title: GDPR: consent defined as freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous
publisher_or_author: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
claim: The EU General Data Protection Regulation defines consent as any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data subject's wishes by statement or clear affirmative action signifying agreement to processing of personal data.
evidence_summary: Article 4(11) GDPR provides a definition of consent requiring a freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data subject's wishes, by a statement or by a clear affirmative action.
source_excerpt: 'consent' of the data subject means any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data subject's wishes by which he or she, by a statement or by a clear affirmative action, signifies agreement to the processing of personal data relating to him or her.
interpretation: Normative evidence of the EU's strict, opt-in consent standard. Useful as an international (EU) comparator standard for consent-based data governance.
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from the primary legal text (Article 4(11)).
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired HTML (source_id=13); locator Article 4(11).

title: GDPR: independent supervisory authorities in each Member State
publisher_or_author: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
claim: The EU General Data Protection Regulation requires each Member State to provide for one or more independent public supervisory authorities responsible for monitoring application of the Regulation, acting with complete independence.
evidence_summary: Articles 51-52 GDPR require Member States to establish one or more independent public authorities (supervisory authorities) to monitor application of the Regulation, and guarantee that these authorities act with complete independence in performing their tasks.
source_excerpt: Each Member State shall provide for one or more independent public authorities to be responsible for monitoring the application of this Regulation... each supervisory authority shall act with complete independence in performing its tasks and exercising its powers in accordance with this Regulation.
interpretation: Normative evidence of the EU's institutional design for data protection oversight, providing an international comparator for supervisory architecture.
methodology_or_basis: Direct quotes from the primary legal text (Articles 51-52).
